newsitem.title: UK: Visa heralds new chip credit card in UK this year.
newsitem.headline: Visa heralds new chip credit card in UK this year.

text.p: Visa International, the credit card company, said on Tuesday that a new, safer, multi-function credit card using state-of-the-art chip programming would be available in Britain in late 1997.

Visa, a service association owned by 20,000 banks worldwide, said the new card would be based on its latest technological breakthrough that allows banks to migrate from common magentic stripe credit cards to chip cards.
"A chip programme offering Visa credit or debit and another programme featuring stored value (in the UK) will be implemented in the autumn of 1997," Visa said.
Called the partnership programme, the new system is supposed to allow banks to customise services to suit individual needs.

Banks can use it to develop their own card with a host of new cash management services including credit and debit facilities, pre-authorised credit levels and can allow customers to collect loyalty points at retail stores.
"We are providing banks with the tools and plantforms to design their own product," Edmund Jensen, president of U.S.-based Visa International, told Reuters.

A chip-based card -- which is already available in South Africa, Spain and South America -- coupled with a speedy telecoms network and a batch of customer services would make banking "an awful lot easier and even more profitable for customers", Jensen said.

The chip technology, developed along with partners such as JavaSoft, IBM (International Business Machines Corp), Motorola Inc, Philips Electronics NV, Siemens AG, makes it easier for banks to combine multiple functions on a single card and maximises space on a chip.
Visa's 561 million cards are accepted at more than 13 million worldwide locations, including nearly 323,000 cash dispensers.
